subject: s14NanInsertedDuringRange
why: a NaN key inserted at each of the first two productions is a NEW entry each time (never found: spec#Comparison_operators), each producible or not, the next inserted only on production — admitted set {12, 23, 33} (members=3; gc exhibits all three); pick-next bound <= 1 candidate + stop

subject: s14NanClearMidRange

subject: s14SignedZeroUpdateMidRange
why: m[-0] = 10 at the first production updates the +0 entry in place (same stamp, still mandatory) and replaces its stored key by -0 (gc: needkeyupdate for floats): the entry is produced first with key +0 and value 1, or later with key -0 and value 10 — admitted set {3001, 3110} (members=2; gc exhibits both); pick-next bound <= 3 candidates + stop

subject: s14InterfaceNanInserted
why: the NaN-in-an-interface twin of nan-inserted-during-range: each insert a new entry, producible or not — admitted set {12, 23, 33} (members=3; gc exhibits all three); pick-next bound <= 1 candidate + stop

subject: s14StructNanKeysMutated
why: struct keys holding NaN mutated at the first production (a new NaN entry inserted, a NaN delete that finds nothing, the non-NaN key updated): three or four productions, the non-NaN key's value read live (30) unless it came first (3), the created entry (4) produced or skipped — admitted set {3006, 3033, 4010, 4037} (members=4; gc exhibits three: the created entry lands behind its cursor when the non-NaN key came first); pick-next bound <= 3 candidates + stop
